input: Write a due diligence memo on Databricks

business.claim: Sells a unified Data + AI Platform for data integration, processing, governance, analytics and AI, built on an open lakehouse architecture.
Serves enterprise technical teams building data and AI applications, while enabling business users to access organizational data through natural-language interfaces.
Products include Lakebase, a serverless Postgres database; Genie Code, an engineering AI agent; Unity Gateway for AI governance and cost controls; and Genie Ontology for organizational context.
Consumption-based business model: pay-as-you-go billing at per-second granularity, with discounted committed-use contracts.
Platform operates across AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.
Company-reported geography, as_of=2026-01-31: headquartered in San Francisco, with more than 35 offices in 22 countries and operations across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
Aggregator Nasdaq Private Market identifies Databricks as privately held, with shares not trading on public exchanges; observed as_of=2026-11-10.

traction.claim: Company claim, as_of=2026-11-10: more than 20,000 organizations and 70% of the Fortune 500 use the platform; named customers include Block, Comcast, Condé Nast, Rivian and Shell.
Company claim, as_of=2026-11-10: ecosystem includes more than 1,200 cloud, independent-software-vendor and consulting partners.
Company claim, as_of=2026-08-13: over 1,000 customers consumed above a $1 million revenue run-rate, including over 100 above $10 million.
Company claim, as_of=2026-02-09: net retention exceeded 140%.
Company claim, jointly announced with FOX: a multi-year partnership designates Databricks as FOX's platform of choice for data, AI applications and agents; FOX's CTO confirms its use.
Company claim, as_of=2026-07-23: Microsoft partnership extended into the 2030s, including deeper integration of Databricks capabilities into Microsoft products and increased internal use of Azure.

team.claim: Company history, observed as_of=2026-11-10: founded in 2013 by Ali Ghodsi, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Patrick Wendell, Reynold Xin, Andy Konwinski and Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji.
Official biography lists co-founder Ali Ghodsi as CEO; he previously led engineering and product management and is affiliated with UC Berkeley.
Official biography lists co-founder Matei Zaharia as CTO and a UC Berkeley associate professor; his technical background includes creating Apache Spark and contributing to MLflow and Delta Lake.
Official speaker biography lists Dave Conte as CFO.
Forbes reported that Conte previously served as CFO of Splunk, Opsware and IronKey, and began his career at Ernst & Young.
October announcement identifies Andy Kofoid as President, Global Field Operations.
Kofoid joined from Salesforce, where he was President of North America; earlier employers included ExactTarget, Dassault Systemes, Oracle and IBM.
April announcement identifies Ron Gabrisko as Chief Revenue Officer and appoints former SAP and Splunk executive Simon Davies as SVP and General Manager for Asia Pacific and Japan.

Notable departure: Bloomberg reported AI head Naveen Rao was leaving his operating role to start another company; Databricks confirmed a transition to an advisory role and planned investment in his startup.

funding.claim: Company-reported, as_of=2026-08-13: closed $5 billion strategic funding at a $190 billion valuation, led by Coatue alongside Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price accounts and Sixth Street Growth. Latest financing valuation verified in this review.

Company-reported, as_of=2026-02-09: Series L financing expanded to approximately $5 billion of equity at a $134 billion valuation, plus approximately $2 billion of additional debt capacity; JPMorgan Chase led the credit facilities.

Company-reported, as_of=2025-12-16: announced Series L exceeding $4 billion at a $134 billion valuation, led by Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research and J.P. Morgan Asset Management. This preceded the February update, not a separate additive round.
Company-reported, as_of=2025-09-08: closing $1 billion Series K at a valuation above $100 billion, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, Insight Partners, MGX, Thrive Capital and WCM Investment Management.

Company-reported, as_of=2025-01-22: closed $10 billion Series J equity at a $62 billion valuation and a $5.25 billion credit facility, comprising a $2.75 billion term loan and $2.5 billion unfunded revolver; Meta joined as a strategic investor.
Series J announcement identified Thrive Capital as lead, with Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, GIC, Insight Partners and WCM Investment Management as co-leads.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim, as_of=2026-08-13: surpassed $7 billion revenue run-rate, growing over 80% year over year during its Q2; this is a run-rate disclosure, not reported full-year revenue.
Company claim, as_of=2026-08-13: positive adjusted free cash flow over the preceding 12 months.
Company claim, as_of=2026-08-13: data warehousing exceeded $1.5 billion revenue run-rate with over 100% annual growth; Lakebase exceeded $100 million revenue run-rate.
Company claim, as_of=2026-02-09: revenue run-rate exceeded $5.4 billion, including $1.4 billion from AI products.
Company headcount claim, as_of=2026-09-28: more than 12,000 people were described as employees in an internal-AI deployment article.
Earlier company headcount claim, as_of=2025-03-06: approximately 8,000 employees; management planned to more than double its San Francisco employee footprint over the following two years.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In In re Mosaic LLM Litigation, the court denied dismissal of authors' amended direct copyright-infringement claim concerning Databricks' DBRX models. This allowed the claim to proceed; it was not a liability determination.
As_of=2026-10-15, the court scheduled the Mosaic litigation's summary-judgment and related motions for December 18, 2026, replacing the October hearing date.

In R2 Solutions LLC v. Databricks, a patent-infringement action, the court struck Databricks' supplemental invalidity contentions and certain expert opinions, and denied its competing motions concerning infringement contentions and claim construction.

TechRadar reported that a Carhartt data leak likely originated from Carhartt's Databricks analytics environment. This was reported customer-environment exposure, not an established compromise of Databricks' corporate systems or shared platform.

SANS relayed Databricks' response to an alleged TeamPCP compromise: the company said its internal investigation found no evidence supporting the information supplied and requested more information. The allegation remained unconfirmed in that report.
Customer agreement requires export-control and sanctions compliance and prohibits access where unlawful. This establishes contractual policy, not verified absence of sanctions exposure.

reputation.claim: Aggregator Glassdoor, as_of=2026-11-10: overall employee rating was 4.0/5 across 1,713 reviews; 77% would recommend the company, while work-life balance rated 3.3/5.

Recent anonymous Glassdoor reviews praised colleagues, products and innovation while repeatedly criticizing workload and work-life balance; one also cited sales pressure. These are self-selected employee accounts.

Aggregator G2, as_of=2026-10-29: rated 4.6/5 across 1,398 reviews. Its review summary identifies recurring learning-curve, complexity and cost-management complaints alongside praise for collaboration and integration.
Critical security coverage linked the reported Carhartt leak to its Databricks environment, creating a reputational diligence issue even though platform-level responsibility was not established.

red_flags.claim: Underwriting concern: as_of=2026-08-13, the $190 billion financing valuation accompanied run-rate revenue and adjusted cash-flow disclosures; obtain recognized-revenue and cash-flow reconciliations.
Copyright exposure: the DBRX infringement claim survived dismissal, warranting review of training-data rights, indemnities and potential litigation reserves.
Patent-defense setback: exclusion of supplemental invalidity contentions and expert opinions in the R2 case warrants specialist review; current disposition and financial exposure were not verified.

Security diligence priority: obtain the root-cause analysis and responsibility allocation for the reported Carhartt customer-environment incident; do not treat it as proof of a corporate Databricks breach.
Inferred adoption risk: recurring customer complaints about complexity, learning requirements and cost management could increase implementation friction and constrain expansion.

output.verdict: Founder-led technical depth, broad enterprise adoption, major distribution partnerships and company-reported growth look strong. Investment underwriting needs closer examination of valuation support, audited revenue and cash economics, copyright and patent exposure, and the reported customer-environment security incident.

cost_basis: tokens x list price + $10 per 1K web search calls
